title: dbt and analytics engineering
summary: A complete SQL-first route from real Core/DuckDB project files through tests, macros, snapshots, incremental correctness, contracts, documentation, targets, state/defer CI, governance and accepted data-product recovery.

lessons.title: A real dbt project and its execution stages
lessons.outcome: Build and inspect a local dbt project through its real adapter.
lessons.lab: Parse, build and query a one-model project to confirm the value 42 in DuckDB, then compile a second model and show that its relation exists only after dbt run.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: A manifest node exists, the database returns 42, and the run result reports success. Worked case 2: Compiled SQL contains 6*7; the answer relation appears only after run.

lessons.title: Seeds, staging and rejected records
lessons.outcome: Create a staging boundary with complete record accounting.
lessons.lab: Seed raw orders, stage them with explicit casts, and show that try_cast accepts two of three rows while the malformed record stays visible in the raw seed.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Three rows materialize and amount totals 21. Worked case 2: Two rows are accepted, one is rejected, and all three remain in raw input.

lessons.title: Dependency graphs and materialization choices
lessons.outcome: Choose a materialization using observed database behavior and a stated workload.
lessons.lab: Build a view and a table that depends on it, read the manifest dependency and the DuckDB object types, then inline an ephemeral model and confirm that no relation is created for it.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: staging is a view, customer_total is a table, and its dependency names staging. Worked case 2: The final answer is 42 and no base relation is created.

lessons.title: Data tests and the meaning of a failed build
lessons.outcome: Use data tests as explicit evidence for a declared contract.
lessons.lab: Declare not_null and unique tests on an order key, build a passing and a duplicated fixture, and repair the duplicate so a full-refresh build passes.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Two test results pass and the table contains two rows. Worked case 2: Duplicate data is rejected by the test; the corrected rebuild passes.

lessons.title: Source freshness and clock assumptions
lessons.outcome: Define and test a source freshness policy with an explicit clock and response.
lessons.lab: Configure a source with a one-hour error_after freshness policy and run dbt source freshness against a current and a two-day-old loaded_at timestamp.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The source freshness status is pass. Worked case 2: The stale source reports error.

lessons.title: Unit fixtures and integration tests
lessons.outcome: Use controlled fixtures to test transformation logic and real-data checks to test integration.
lessons.lab: Run a YAML unit test with its own two-row input, confirm that the production seed is unchanged, and make a deliberately wrong expected row fail.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The unit test passes with total 5 and the source seed is unchanged. Worked case 2: The unit result is fail under the incorrect expected row.

lessons.title: Jinja macros and compiled SQL evidence
lessons.outcome: Review a macro through its source, emitted SQL and actual result.
lessons.lab: Write a safe_ratio macro, compare its compiled CASE expression with the materialized rates 0.25 and null, and confirm that an undefined macro fails at compilation.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The rates are 0.25 and null; compiled SQL contains CASE logic rather than the macro call. Worked case 2: Compilation fails before model execution.

lessons.title: Incremental watermarks and late-arriving records
lessons.outcome: State the assumptions under which an incremental result equals a full recomputation.
lessons.lab: Run a max-watermark incremental model through an append and a repeat run, then add a late record behind the watermark and compare the incremental result with a full refresh.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Two records remain after the append and repeat run. Worked case 2: The incremental relation has 2 rows; full refresh has 3.

lessons.title: Keyed updates, lookback windows and idempotency
lessons.outcome: Implement a keyed incremental contract with tested boundary and repeat-run behavior.
lessons.lab: Apply a delete+insert model with a ten-unit lookback to a correction and a late insert, rerun it without duplicates, and show that a record outside the window needs a full refresh.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Final amounts are id 1=6, id 2=7 and id 3=9, with three rows after rerun. Worked case 2: Normal output has 1 row; a declared full refresh produces 2.

lessons.title: Snapshots and observed historical state
lessons.outcome: Explain what a snapshot actually observed and what it cannot reconstruct.
lessons.lab: Snapshot a customer seed with the check strategy and hard_deletes set to invalidate, change one region, and compare history rows with current rows after a deletion.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: There are 3 history rows; current regions are west and south. Worked case 2: History still has 3 rows, but only customer 1/west is current.

lessons.title: Enforced model schemas and constraint boundaries
lessons.outcome: Define a model schema contract and verify both accepted and rejected changes.
lessons.lab: Enforce a model contract with declared column types, build a compatible model, then change its output type and confirm that the run fails while the earlier relation keeps 42.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The model returns id 1 and amount 42 under the declared types. Worked case 2: The incompatible run fails and the previous valid amount remains 42.

lessons.title: Model versions and semantic compatibility
lessons.outcome: Manage a semantic model change with explicit consumer versioning.
lessons.lab: Publish two versions of a model, query a consumer pinned to version 1 and one that follows the latest version, and name the gross-to-net change that separates 100 from 80.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The explicit v1 consumer returns 100; the latest v2 consumer returns 80. Worked case 2: Net is 80, derived from gross 100 and returns 20.

lessons.title: Selectors, graph expansion and state comparison
lessons.outcome: Construct and inspect a reproducible selection against an explicit baseline.
lessons.lab: List the models selected by tag:feature+, then save a manifest, change one model and select state:modified+ against that saved baseline.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The selected model names are base and child. Worked case 2: Changed and downstream selection contains both models.

lessons.title: Documentation, catalogs, exposures and ownership
lessons.outcome: Build documentation that joins observed structure with authored meaning and ownership.
lessons.lab: Generate documentation for a described mart with an exposure, read the catalog and manifest, and detect a model whose type is known but whose description is missing.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The catalog contains total and the decision-report exposure depends on mart. Worked case 2: The type is available, but the business description is missing.

lessons.title: Publication gates after materialization
lessons.outcome: Separate candidate computation from accepted publication.
lessons.lab: Build a candidate relation and record publication only when every test passes, then show that a failed uniqueness test leaves the candidate built but unpublished.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Two candidate rows are present and publication is true. Worked case 2: Two candidate rows exist, but publication is false.

lessons.title: Metric contracts and valid denominators
lessons.outcome: Publish a metric with a complete numerator/denominator contract and an independent check.
lessons.lab: Compute pooled cohort rates in SQL from success and trial counts, check them against independent arithmetic, and compare an equal-row average that differs by more than 0.4.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Cohort A is 0.1 from 100 trials; cohort B is 0.5 from 2 trials. Worked case 2: Equal-row averaging differs by more than 0.4 from the pooled rate.

lessons.title: Temporal data products and late-known facts
lessons.outcome: Produce a historical feature relation with explicit entity, time and version semantics.
lessons.lab: Build a point-in-time feature model that requires event and known times to precede each request cutoff, and compare it with an event-time-only model that returns 999.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The available feature values are [10, 30]. Worked case 2: The event-only model returns [999, 30].

lessons.title: Local packages and reusable project dependencies
lessons.outcome: Prepare and inspect a real reusable dbt dependency with an explicit source boundary.
lessons.lab: Prepare a local package with dbt deps, use its add_one macro in a model that returns 42, and show that compiling before the package is prepared fails.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The macro is registered, the lockfile is written and the model returns 42. Worked case 2: Missing dependency preparation fails; local deps followed by compile succeeds.

lessons.title: Targets, environments and owned database routing
lessons.outcome: Run a project against an explicitly identified owned target and verify its actual destination.
lessons.lab: Add dev and prod outputs to the profile, build one model into both schemas with its target name, and confirm that an unknown target is rejected before any model runs.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: dev.answer and prod.answer contain the corresponding target label and 42. Worked case 2: The unknown target is rejected before a successful model run.

lessons.title: Deferral and the choice of upstream state
lessons.outcome: Use deferral with an explicit upstream-state contract.
lessons.lab: Build a prod baseline, save its manifest and run a dev child with --defer and --state, then add a stale dev parent and compare the default result with --favor-state.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The child returns 11 and its parent is resolved from prod. Worked case 2: The default result is 101; favor-state produces 2.

lessons.title: Slim CI with actual builds and data tests
lessons.outcome: Implement a reproducible reduced CI workflow with explicit selection, baseline and ownership.
lessons.lab: Build a prod baseline, save its manifest, change the child model and run a state:modified+ build in dev for a compatible change and for a change that duplicates rows.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The changed candidate passes and the accepted baseline is unchanged. Worked case 2: The candidate contains a failed test and the baseline still has one row.

lessons.title: Diagnose template, database and semantic failures
lessons.outcome: Diagnose failures using the layer that actually rejected the work.
lessons.lab: Compile a model whose SQL the database rejects and read its error status, then build a model with a wrong factor of 2 and catch it with a singular reconciliation test.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Compiled SQL exists, but the model result status is error. Worked case 2: The relation contains 24 and the independent reconciliation test fails.

lessons.title: Query plans, measured cost and semantic equivalence
lessons.outcome: Measure database work with a correctness oracle and a clearly defined interval.
lessons.lab: Time a grouped query whose five totals are checked against Python arithmetic, then show that a select distinct rewrite changes the total from 17 to 12.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The five group totals match Python arithmetic and a nonnegative timing summary is reported. Worked case 2: The multiset total is 17; the changed result totals 12.

lessons.title: Groups, model access and governance boundaries
lessons.outcome: Use groups and model access to define supported project interfaces, while keeping database authorization claims separate.
lessons.lab: Declare two groups and a private model, build a consumer in the same group, and confirm that dbt rejects a consumer in another group that references the private model.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The build succeeds, while direct SQL visibility remains a separate fact. Worked case 2: The cross-group private-model reference is rejected.

lessons.title: Recovery, accepted versions and atomic pointers
lessons.outcome: Recover a data product through explicit accepted versions and a tested pointer mechanism.
lessons.lab: Change an accepted-version pointer inside a DuckDB transaction and roll it back, then reject a candidate that fails a value test while the accepted value stays 42.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The temporary 99 is visible inside the transaction; rollback restores version 1/value 42. Worked case 2: The candidate is rejected and the accepted value remains 42.

lessons.title: Publish a complete validated analytics product
lessons.outcome: Deliver a complete local analytics product with a reviewable acceptance decision.
lessons.lab: Build staging and mart models with key tests, write a publication receipt for customer totals 12 and 9, and block publication when the customer dimension has a duplicate key.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Customer totals are 12 and 9, overall 21; one raw order is quarantined and a receipt is written. Worked case 2: The invalid candidate is not published.
